input.situation_text: Contractor reported window handle job complete and said invoice attached, but the invoice attachment isn't visible. System flagged 3+ reminders sent to provider. Landlord approved without an amount.

lessons.situation: A contractor emails to say a job is complete and attaches a completion photo and invoice, but the attachments are unavailable or unreadable, and the system has flagged the case to check whether a reply to the provider is needed or to return it to auto mode.
lessons.action: Treat the contractor's completion email as no further reply needed to the provider. Move the task to the result stage, mark the request completed and start the final checks. If the completion photo or invoice could not be opened or isn't required, record a reason for skipping the document upload. Then flag the case for landlord confirmation before closing, and return the request to auto mode rather than chasing the contractor.
lessons.rationale: A clear completion confirmation from the contractor does not need a response, and the remaining closeout step is landlord sign-off, which automation can continue once the request is back in auto mode.

lessons.situation: A contractor who missed a confirmed appointment and was rebooked has emailed to report the plumbing job completed (part replaced, tenants confirming the other fault is fine), while the request was on hold awaiting the provider and flagged to check whether a response is needed before returning to auto mode.
lessons.action: When a contractor reports completion after a rescheduled or missed visit, confirm the report covers all reported faults and that the tenant has not raised any outstanding issue. If no reply to the contractor is needed, record that the landlord pays the contractor directly, close the task as completed without agency payment, and return the request to auto mode.
lessons.rationale: A completion report that addresses every fault needs no further chasing, and noting the landlord's direct payment arrangement keeps the agency from processing an invoice it will not pay.

lessons.situation: After the system auto-sent appointment confirmations for a repair, the tenant phoned to say the date in the notifications conflicted with the date they had already agreed directly with the contractor, and asked which was correct.
lessons.action: Reply to the tenant to apologise for the confusion and tell them the date they agreed directly with the contractor is the one to follow, rather than the date in the automated notification. Then put the job on hold with the reason 'Waiting for Provider' so the contractor can confirm the date, instead of returning it to auto mode.
lessons.rationale: Automated confirmations can be sent with a date that does not match what the contractor and tenant arranged directly, so the contractor's agreed date should take priority and the job should wait for the provider's confirmation before automation resumes.

lessons.situation: After chasing a landlord for approval of a high-cost specialist waste removal quote, the landlord replies approving the work, and the request has been flagged by the system to check whether a response is needed or to return it to auto mode.
lessons.action: Treat the landlord's approval as the go-ahead: do not return the request to auto mode yet. Instruct the contractor to arrange the removal and keep the job on hold with a note that it is being arranged. Then contact the tenant straight away with the contractor's available dates to arrange access, asking for prompt confirmation. If phone calls go unanswered, follow up in writing, and switch the hold reason to waiting for the tenant once the access request has been sent.
lessons.rationale: Landlord approval removes the blocker, but the job still needs contractor booking and tenant access confirmed, so it needs active human-style coordination rather than being handed back to automation.

lessons.situation: A repair was carried out by a provider under warranty, the tenant confirmed the fix appeared to work, and the provider emailed confirming completion at no charge, after the job had been held awaiting the provider and the system prompted a check on whether any response was needed.
lessons.action: Treat the provider's completion email as final confirmation, record a brief note that the repair was done under warranty with no charge, mark the task completed without payment, and return the request to auto mode. Do not send a reply to the provider or contact the landlord, as no response or approval is needed.
lessons.rationale: A warranty repair with tenant confirmation and no cost leaves nothing to approve, pay or chase, so the correct step is to document it and close the job cleanly instead of generating unnecessary communication.
